summary: Modern mainstream pop: 100-125 BPM, punchy programmed drums with a clap on 2 and 4, a synth bass on the roots, four-chord loops (I-V-vi-IV) on piano or synths, a short bright hook; knowledge/style/pop.json is its template
body: Tempo 100-125 BPM, most hits 100-120; slower drifts to ballad, faster to dance or hyperpop.

Drums: programmed and tight: a punchy kick, a snappy snare layered with (or replaced by) a clap on 2 and 4, crisp straight 8th or 16th hats; 808 and 909 sounds are common. Big long clean reverbs for shimmer, not on the kick.
Bass: a synth bass is the most common choice (else an electric bass or an 808), on the roots following the kick, sidechained to it.
Harmony: simple triads looped, four chords (I-V-vi-IV, vi-IV-I-V; minor i-VI-III-VII); a chord every 2 beats in a verse, a full bar each in the chorus for weight; piano, plucks or synth pads.
Lead: the vocal topline; as an instrument, a bright clear synth lead or pluck with a short, repeated, singable hook.
Texture/master: clean, bright, loud and wide; polished top end, controlled low end; no lofi roll-off.

Sources (2026-11-26): MusicRadar 'Songwriting basics: how to create a modern pop song using just 4 chords' and '25 pop tips'; UJAM 'How To Make Modern Pop Drums'; Soundtrap 'How To Make Pop Music'; eMastered 'How to Make a Pop Beat'.
Apply: pattern/gmd-pop-beat-1 on the drums, then pattern/pop-i-v-vi-iv on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/pop.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
